title: Technician groups collapse and expand, and stay that way for the user
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on the Work Orders build under test with Work Orders view permission; the Board View and Tech View display options are on.
  2. The current location has at least 3 lead technicians shown as groups/columns (a technician is eligible when they are Clockable, Active, and their role is not Office or Time Clock User).
  3. Via New Work Order, create several work orders and set a Lead Technician on each, spread across the technicians with some left Unassigned; then open the Work Orders page.
  4. Location has several eligible technicians (Clockable, Active, role not Office / not Time Clock User, enrolled here) and seeded work orders spread across statuses (Estimate, Approved, In Progress, Review/Ready for Review, Complete, Invoiced, Paid, Declined, Imported), including at least one with no lead technician.
  5. In Tech View.
custom_steps:
1. Collapse a technician group and expand another.
  2. Refresh the page.
  3. Open a new tab to Work Orders.
  4. Log out and back in.
  5. Confirm the collapsed/expanded states are restored each time.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Each technician group can be collapsed and expanded.
  • A group's collapsed/expanded state is remembered per user across sessions, logout/login, refreshes, new tabs, and reopening.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043 (Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options). Story reference: SV-10045 — Tech View. Spec: Confluence page 845185030 “Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options”, PRD v33 (2026-09-28), requirement(s) S2-R5, S2-R13 (read 30 Sep 2026). Review decisions/answers: Confluence page 853901313 where cited. Source-verified on 30 September 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S2-R5: “Allow each technician group to be collapsed or expanded.”
  • S2-R13: “Save group collapse state per user. It is kept after refreshes, logout/login, new tabs, and reopening the page.”
